correctness.rationale: The only imported non-elementary statement is the 2022 theorem reducing worst-case phase-retrieval stability to orthogonal vectors. For an arbitrary orthogonal pair, the three Mercedes measurements give the exact identity \(D^2=\tfrac32(r^2+s^2)-rsL(2\theta)\). The periodic absolute-sine sum satisfies \(L\le2\) by a one-interval trigonometric calculation, yielding the global lower Lipschitz constant \(1/\sqrt2\). The explicit unit orthogonal pair \((1,1)/\sqrt2\), \((-1,1)/\sqrt2\) attains equality. No finite computation is extrapolated to the global statement.

originality.rationale: Six targeted semantic searches were run for the exact frame, lower-Lipschitz/condition-number aliases, orthogonal-pair reduction, and strong-complement formulations. The relevant published and indexed literature was compared for Mercedes-frame and phase-retrieval stability overlap. The full relevant 2022 and 2013 primary texts were inspected, and the 2008 primary article was inspected around its Mercedes example and reconstruction framework. Those sources supply the object and general machinery but not the sharp frame-specific value established here. One dissertation indexed with a Mercedes-frame figure could not be materially inspected beyond index metadata and is recorded as a residual risk.
residual_risks: The inaccessible dissertation indexed as CORE:236315327 could contain the same exact Mercedes-frame stability computation; only its index metadata was available.
An unindexed thesis, lecture note, or informal calculation could state the same sharp constant under equivalent normalization.
Different frame scalings change the numerical stability constant, so comparisons require normalization to unit-norm Mercedes vectors and Euclidean magnitude measurements.

value.rationale: The Mercedes frame is the canonical real three-vector equiangular tight frame and a standard phase-retrieval measurement system in dimension two. Because three measurements are the minimal cardinality for real phase retrieval in \(\mathbb{R}^2\), its exact global conditioning is a natural benchmark. The result gives a sharp self-contained invariant with an equality configuration and a short structural proof enabled by the 2022 orthogonal reduction; it is not merely a frame-bound recomputation.
